 PARASTAR Takes BIG OCEAN Beyond the Stage With Inclusive K-Pop Fan Travel in Korea
 by 
 Zee Cindy 
 post_date_format( $post ) ); ?> 
 --> 
 November 6, 2026 
 in 
 Press Release 
 0 
 For international K-pop fans, visiting South Korea offers the chance to experience the culture behind their favorite music. But spending meaningful time with the artists they admire often involves coordinating concerts, fan events, and travel arrangements separately . And while that may be just another day for regular K-poppers, for fans with disabilities , additional accessibility considerations can make that journey even more complicated.
 Now, what if a K-pop trip could bring these experiences together? And fans will be able to share activities with their favorite artists while exploring Korea?
 Seoul-based PARASTAR Entertainment is bringing this vision to life through BIG OCEAN , a three-member K-pop group featuring artists with hearing disabilities . The company is expanding its artist management and intellectual property (IP) business into an inclusive K-pop fan tourism program, creating opportunities for international fans to experience Korean culture through direct artist interactions, accessibility-conscious activities, and shared experiences. 
 In October 2026, PARASTAR brought this concept into practice through “WELCOME TO OUR HOME,” a three-day, two-night fan travel pilot in Chuncheon that brought together 14 participants, including international fans from five countries . The experience marked an important step toward transforming BIG OCEAN’s growing global fandom into a new tourism business opportunity. 
 From Discovering Artists With Disabilities to Building Global K-Pop IP
 Founded in 2020 by CEO Haley Cha , a former YTN news anchor, PARASTAR Entertainment began with a mission to create professional opportunities for talented individuals with disabilities. 
 The idea emerged in 2018, when Cha attended an event commemorating the 30th anniversary of the Seoul Paralympic Games . She encountered athletes with strong talent and public appeal who were receiving television and advertising opportunities but lacked professional representation to manage contracts and negotiate appearance fees.
 Recognizing the gap between talent and commercial opportunity , Cha established PARASTAR as an agency connecting artists with disabilities to broadcasting and advertising projects . The business subsequently evolved into an entertainment company focused on artist discovery, professional development, content production, and IP commercialization. 
 Today, PARASTAR works with more than 40 artists with disabilities across music, broadcasting, advertising, and live performances. BIG OCEAN represents a significant step in that evolution, demonstrating how professionally developed artist IP can connect with international audiences through music and live entertainment. 
 The group incorporates Korean Sign Language (KSL), American Sign Language (ASL), and International Sign (IS) into its performances, creating a distinctive artistic identity that connects music, sign language, and global fan engagement.
 BIG OCEAN. | PARASTAR 
 Building on BIG OCEAN’s international performances and collaborations, PARASTAR is now exploring how that relationship with fans can extend into tourism. 
 WELCOME TO OUR HOME Brings Fans and Artists Together in Korea
 A K-pop concert lets fans watch their favorite artists perform. But what if they could also share a picnic, enjoy a friendly sports competition, and create memories together in Korea? PARASTAR is bringing this more personal fan experience to life through its BIG OCEAN tourism initiative. 
 In October 2026, PARASTAR conducted a proof-of-concept (PoC) for its three-day, two-night “WELCOME TO OUR HOME” fan travel program . The experience brought together 14 participants , including 11 international fans from China, Germany, Sweden, France, and Brazil, two Korean fans, and one artist with a disability represented by PARASTAR. 
 At a campsite in Chuncheon, South Korea, participants enjoyed a series of activities with BIG OCEAN, including sports competitions, a mini concert by the group, a campfire, and a treasure hunt .
 Designed to evoke the familiar atmosphere of a Korean school trip, the program offered international fans a more personal way to connect with their favorite artists while experiencing Korean culture beyond the concert stage. 
 The pilot also provided PARASTAR with practical insights into fan preferences, travel demand, operational requirements, and safety management . Building on these experiences, the company is now planning seasonal fan travel products that could bring more international visitors to Korea through shared experiences with K-pop artists.
 “Rather than simply visiting tourist attractions or attending concerts, we want fans and artists to spend time together and naturally experience the values of inclusion that BIG OCEAN conveys,”
 explained CEO Haley Cha.
 CEO Haley Cha. | PARASTAR 
 Accessibility is also central to PARASTAR’s tourism approach. PARASTAR brings experience in arranging sign language interpreters, managing ADA-designated accessibility zones, assisting audience members with disabilities, and organizing barrier-free events. The company applies this expertise to its tourism planning by considering participants’ accessibility needs, travel routes, and appropriate interpretation support for each program.
 Alongside its camping initiative, BIG OCEAN was appointed a 2026 Open Tourism Ambassador by the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO). Through this appointment, PARASTAR worked with KTO to conduct proof-of-concept activities for barrier-free fan tourism , exploring how accessible travel could become part of the K-pop fan experience. 
 The activities included a sign-language walking tour in Suwon accompanied by sign language interpreters and a barrier-free tour in Gangneung designed to accommodate travelers with mobility limitations .
 These experiences allowed PARASTAR to extend its accessibility-conscious approach beyond entertainment venues, demonstrating how fans can explore Korean destinations together regardless of disability status.
 Not only that, but the company is also developing future travel activities incorporating plogging , an environmentally friendly activity combining outdoor exercise with litter collection . By bringing together K-pop, meaningful artist interactions, accessibility, and sustainability, PARASTAR aims to make visiting Korea an experience that celebrates both fandom and inclusion. 
 PARASTAR Secures KRW 1 Billion Through Tourism Global Challenge
 PARASTAR’s expansion into fan tourism builds on its established entertainment operations and investment history.
 The company previously attracted investment from Hana Ventures and Korea Social Investment in 2022, MYSC and CNT Tech in 2023, and additional funding from CNT Tech in 2025. In 2026, PARASTAR secured KRW 1 billion in investment from the Chungnam–NCK Digital Tourism Fund through the 2026 Tourism Global Challenge’s investment IR program , marking an important financial milestone as the company develops its artist-led fan tourism business.
 In May 2023, PARASTAR also obtained B Corp certification , achieving a score of 100.2 in B Lab’s impact assessment , reflecting its commitment to pursuing social value alongside sustainable business development.
 Its existing revenue model includes performance and appearance contracts, album and digital music sales, official merchandise, and artist IP activities. Concert organizers and brands pay contracted appearance and collaboration fees, while fans purchase tickets, albums, and merchandise.
 Tourism presents an additional avenue for developing BIG OCEAN’s IP beyond traditional entertainment activities. PARASTAR intends to refine its tourism products’ operational and sales models while exploring collaboration opportunities with travel industry partners .
 Expanding Inclusive K-Pop Tourism Through International Partnerships
 With BIG OCEAN connecting with fans around the world, PARASTAR is looking to bring its inclusive K-pop tourism experiences to a wider international audience . Through the 2026 Tourism Global Challenge , the company is building relationships with international tourism and business networks to explore new opportunities for artist-driven travel experiences.
 In August 2026, PARASTAR participated in a networking event in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam , introducing its artist IP business and exploring collaboration opportunities in Asian markets. The experience marked another step toward connecting its entertainment expertise with international tourism and distribution networks.
 The company is particularly interested in partnerships with concert promoters and fan experience travel agencies in the United States and Europe , as well as tourism and distribution operators across Asia, including Vietnam.
 PARASTAR brings together BIG OCEAN’s artist IP, performance and content production expertise, international fan connections, and experience in accessibility-conscious event operations . Potential tourism partners could complement these strengths through local sales networks, travel arrangements, accommodation, and transportation services, creating opportunities to develop engaging and accessible K-pop travel products for international visitors.
 BIG OCEAN. | PARASTAR 
 Building the Next Chapter of BIG OCEAN Fan Travel
 With its initial fan travel and barrier-free tourism pilots completed, PARASTAR is turning its operational experience into plans for a sustainable, seasonal K-pop tourism business . The company is using insights into fan demand, accessibility, participant safety, and program management to develop travel experiences that can be refined and expanded over time.
 Over the next 12 months, PARASTAR aims to build on the results of “WELCOME TO OUR HOME” and its collaboration with the Korea Tourism Organization, exploring new experiences that combine K-pop artist interactions with South Korea’s cultural attractions and tourism destinations . It also plans to strengthen partnerships with international travel and content industry operators to support future tourism product development and market expansion.
 For PARASTAR, BIG OCEAN’s journey is expanding beyond music and performances into shared experiences that bring artists and fans closer together. By combining its global fandom, entertainment expertise, and commitment to accessibility, the company aims to create new opportunities for Korean tourism while developing a business where meaningful artist-fan connections become part of the travel experience. 
 PARASTAR Entertainment is participating in the 2026 TOURISM GLOBAL CHALLENGE program, an initiative led by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism of the Republic of Korea and the Korea Tourism Organization to support promising Korean tourism companies seeking to expand into global markets.
